title: Fix t3 trigger wording and make the decider test structural
summary: Retry of the rejected job. Make the t3 trigger in model.json say only what its cited claims support, and replace the prefix-match decider test in xtask/src/site.rs with a structural check backed by a model field. The audience is the newcomer reading the published study page, and the verifier who checks it.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check must pass, with positive and negative fixtures.
The decider rule is enforced by a structural check on a model field, not by a text prefix.
Criteria require fixtures that the check rejects or accepts, and a run of the site build.
Behavior criteria name the commands the verifier can run.
The wording is plain and the changelog is accurate.
Only the t3 wording, the test, and the changelog change.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The request means the introspection's proposed next request: fix the two remaining findings (t3 wording, structural decider test).
A structural check needs a model field. I assume an optional 'trigger_actor' string is added to each transition and the schema or validator accepts it; if one already exists, the producer reuses it.

t3 will be reworded so the actor is the worker or a script, as the claims (c3, c31, c37) say, with trigger_evaluated_by changed to match. If no claim says the agent accepts the report, the producer must not keep the agent as the subject.
The earlier JSON spacing fix on t3, t8, t10 and t11 and the in-scope glossary entry already landed or carry over unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: In model.json the t3 trigger names only an event that a claim it cites supports (c3, c31, c37). It does not say the agent accepts or records the worker's report unless a cited claim says so. Its trigger_evaluated_by value matches the actor the claims name.
The model records each transition's trigger actor in a field, not in the trigger text. Every cited claim id exists in claims.json.

Run cargo test. The site test checks structurally, with no text prefix or keyword ban: for each transition with trigger_evaluated_by 'agent', the actor field says agent, and every cited claim id resolves. All tests pass.

Run cargo test. A fixture with an agent-evaluated transition whose trigger describes another actor's event is rejected by the check, and a fixture with a valid agent trigger passes. The tests assert both outcomes.

Run cargo run -p xtask -- site. The study builds and validates, and the generated page keeps the in-scope glossary entry and a next-step link before the first transition card. It has no f2/f3 model-limit note.
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are clean.
The CHANGELOG.md entry describes only what was done and does not overclaim.

out_of_scope: Changing how much of the page is about Athena rather than firstmate

departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass probability than the reference. The previous attempt failed on the same two points, and the work touches the model schema and a test.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time from a rejected attempt: the retry gets a structural check and fixtures, so the same two findings are caught before the final verdict.
